scenario: A child will closely inspect a vetted Moon photo.
input: Make a look-notice-wonder page for a real Moon crater photo.
must: Large photo, notice space, wonder space.

scenario: A child will bring one real leaf to the table.
input: Make a page to look closely at a leaf we collect, draw a detail, and wonder.
must: Work with the real object and generous drawing space.

scenario: A child compares two paper airplane wing shapes.
input: Make a page to circle clues and explain how wide and narrow wings flew differently.
must: Side-by-side comparison and one explanation.

scenario: A child compares two real rocks.
input: Make a compare page for two rocks: color, sparkle, edges, and texture.
must: Circle evidence and explain one difference.

scenario: A child matches ordinary tools to jobs.
input: Make a two-column page matching tape, ruler, crayon, and scissors to their jobs.
must: Two complete shuffled sets and safe scissor note.

scenario: A child matches animal tracks to animals.
input: Make a tiny matching page for duck, rabbit, dog, and deer tracks.
must: Complete separate item sets.
must_not: No answer embedded in each choice.

scenario: A child sorts picture-word cards by plant part.
input: Make cards to sort foods into roots and leaves.
must: Movable cards and visible category areas.

scenario: A child predicts which household objects might float or sink.
input: Make cut-apart cards to sort into my float and sink predictions.
must: Prediction categories and cards; actual test remains separate.
must_not: Do not print an answer key as guaranteed for every material.

scenario: A child orders four butterfly stages.
input: Make movable story cards for egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly.
must: Four accurate movable steps.

scenario: A child practices a routine with five visual steps.
input: Make five simple handwashing cards we can put in order.
must: Five usable ordered actions and grown-up check.

scenario: A child labels a simplified insect body.
input: Make a big diagram to label head, thorax, abdomen, antennae, and legs.
must: Accurate code-owned central diagram and callouts inside the printable.
must_not: No model-generated anatomy and no duplicate standalone diagram.

scenario: A child labels parts on their own drawn boat.
input: Make a page where my child draws a boat and labels hull, sail, mast, and rudder.
must: Large drawing space and clear label prompts.
must_not: No need for decorative sea art.

scenario: A child observes signs of insects outdoors.
input: Make a backyard insect clue checklist: holes, webs, chewed leaves, and tiny tracks.
must: Visible clue checkboxes and drawing space.

scenario: A child records weather clues without instruments.
input: Make a window weather checklist for clouds, moving branches, puddles, and shadows.
must: Simple checks and one wonder.

scenario: A child predicts and tests which ramp height makes a toy car travel farther.
input: Make a predict-test-record page for two safe cardboard ramp heights.
must: Fair comparison and result space.

scenario: A child predicts and observes ice in two locations.
input: Make a page to predict and record which ice cube melts first: shade or sun.
must: Prediction, safe test, and two result spaces.
must_not: Do not state the child's result in advance.

scenario: A child records three throws for two plane designs.
input: Make a tally and dot graph page for six paper airplane flights.
must: Named repeated trials and a simple graph.
must_not: Do not ask parent to create the table.

scenario: A child tallies birds seen in short observation windows.
input: Make a tally-and-graph page for robin, sparrow, crow, and other.
must: Clear tally categories and graph area.
must_not: No pressure to identify uncertain birds.

scenario: A child builds, tests, and improves one foil boat.
input: Make a build-test-improve page for a small foil boat and pennies.
must: Sketch, safe test, change one thing, retest.
must_not: No 3D printer or exact promised capacity.

scenario: A child designs a small paper shelter for a toy.
input: Make a page to sketch, test with a fan, and improve a paper shelter.
must: Mission, constraints, test, and revision.

scenario: A child solves a playful evidence mystery.
input: Make a case file: which stuffed animal moved the pretend snack?
must: Clues, suspects, best solution, evidence.
must_not: Do not imply a real child did something wrong.

scenario: A child identifies one of three common seeds from visible clues.
input: Make a seed detective case using size, shape, and texture clues.
must: Observable clues and uncertainty-friendly solution.
must_not: No tasting or exact identification from weak evidence.

scenario: A child watches a common animal from a window.
input: Make a squirrel mini field guide for tail, paws, ears, and movement.
must: Vetted photo, field marks, and detail drawing.

scenario: A child compares visible bark and leaf clues on one local tree.
input: Make a mini field guide page we can use with a real tree outside.
must: Field marks and drawing space; identification may remain uncertain.
must_not: Do not invent species from location-free context.

scenario: A parent wants a quick spoken answer while leaving home.
input: We are walking out the door. Just tell me why shadows move; no activity or page.
must: Direct short answer.
